A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same VideoWorld study, with 15 pages including references and Appendices A–B. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Go gameplay and robotic-control results in Tables 1–3, ablations in Tables 4–5, and board-state analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results and analyses, including the Go and robotics evaluations, ablations, and Appendix B.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same video-generation framework, latent dynamics model, inverse dynamics model, training objectives, and inference procedures. Algorithm 1 is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Video-GoBench, CALVIN, and RLBench with the same Go, block-pushing, drawer, lighting, microwave-closing, and fridge-closing tasks. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same comparator membership: the three KataGo skill levels, state/video Transformer comparisons, MCIL, HULC, and oracle models in their respective experiments.

E3.justification: The published protocols are unchanged, including 400 Go games per agent pair, the CALVIN ABCD-to-D split, 500 sampled robotic tasks, model sizes, and training settings.

E4.justification: The horizon, codebook, data-source, code-intervention, and prediction-target analyses remain unchanged, as do the latent-code visualizations and Appendix B board-state overlap analysis. Page 10 redisplays the same qualitative examples with adjusted spacing.

E5.justification: Both retain the same BayesElo procedure, stated confidence of 0.5, and Elo uncertainty reporting in Table 1. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 reports VideoWorld 300M at 2317 ±25 Elo in both versions under the same settings.

T1.justification: The task formulation, conditional video-generation model, latent-code definitions, and action mappings in Section 3 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about learning knowledge from videos, the importance of compact visual-change representations, VideoWorld's Go performance, and robotic generalization.

C2.justification: The interpretations connecting latent codes to planning, explanations of horizon/codebook convergence failures, and limitations concerning real-world generation quality and generalization are unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.1, Appendix A, Table A.1, and Algorithm 1 retain the same hyperparameters, hardware, training times, data-generation instructions, and implementation details. The project URL and code/data/model availability statements also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 75 numbered references are unchanged. The positioning relative to video generation, knowledge learning, and latent-action methods is retained.

P1.justification: v2 removes the University of Science and Technology of China affiliation, renumbers affiliation superscripts, updates the arXiv version/date stamp, and capitalizes the 'Auto-regressive Transformer' heading. The narrative and section structure otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adjusts first-page vertical spacing and the placement of Figures 7–9 and their captions on page 10. Moving Figure 7(b) downward exposes the previously covered Figure 7(a) label. The figure images and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v1's second Go panel covers the Figure 7(a) label; v2 separates the panels so the label is readable, making the strategy visualization easier to follow. This provides a limited presentation improvement, while the scientific content, evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
